reason: The Moon’s differing pull on Earth’s near and far sides is the physical starting point for tides.

choice.combine: The Moon with a pale early crust

expectation: This should reveal the unequal lunar pull that drives tides.

effect: The Moon’s uneven pull is now available as the starting point for the tidal process.
reaction: The distinction between differential gravity and a simple upward pull is useful.
reason: The uneven pull should act on the sea to produce a tidal response.
expectation: The sea will develop a tidal response to the Moon’s uneven gravity.

effect: The uneven pull produces a tide moving through the sea, rather than a fixed mound of water.
reason: The shallow seabed should shape the tide as it reaches the coast.

choice.combine: A tide moving through the sea

expectation: The tide will be altered as it moves into shallow coastal water.

effect: The moving tide is now shaped into a local coastal tide by the seabed.
reaction: The reminder that local geography matters is useful.
reason: The local tide should flood and drain the beach.

choice.with: A dark beach in the sheltered bay

expectation: The beach will become a shore alternately covered and exposed by the tide.

effect: The rising tide has covered the beach; the draining phase remains to be shown.
reaction: The distinction between waves and the slower tide is useful.
reason: I expect Earth’s rotation to help advance the local tidal cycle toward falling water.
expectation: The tide will recede and expose the beach again.

effect: The falling tide exposed the beach and completed the flooding-and-draining goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the same shore pass through both tidal states.
reason: Raised rims should retain some water in rock hollows as the tide falls.

choice.combine: A beach exposed by the falling tide

expectation: Sheltered pools of seawater will remain in the hollows.

effect: The raised rock rims retained water as the tide withdrew, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It is satisfying that the pools follow naturally from the shape of the shore.

mostWorthwhile.text: Shaping the moving tide with the coastal seabed was worthwhile: it connected lunar gravity to the important role of local geography.

leastWorthwhile.text: Flooding and then exposing the beach were predictable steps, though they clearly showed the two states of the same shore.

surprise.text: The explanation that tides travel through ocean basins, rather than forming a fixed mound following the Moon, changed my picture of the process.

arbitrary.text: Combining the flooded beach with the rotating Earth felt somewhat abstract, even though I expected it to advance the tidal cycle.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see more natural processes connected to familiar features of the coast, especially with the same attention to local conditions.
